chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn al-Nahdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits his brother for the sake of Allah and for Allah, will come on the Day of Resurrection striding between gowns of light, and not pass by anything except that it shines for him, until he stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to him: 'Welcome!' And when He says 'Welcome', Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will bestow upon him abundant gifts.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother in faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that ziarah (visitation) is not merely social but a spiritual bond rooted in divine love (mawaddah). The imagery of 'walking between curtains of light' (qabatiyyah) signifies the high status of the believer in the Hereafter, while the specific divine utterance 'Marhaban' indicates a personalized, generous reception that surpasses general greetings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and communal aspects of faith.
